display.fontFamily: IBM Plex Sans, Noto Sans Thai Looped, system-ui, sans-serif
display.purpose: Page titles and high-level report titles only.

body.fontFamily: IBM Plex Sans, Noto Sans Thai Looped, system-ui, sans-serif
body.purpose: Dense Thai and English UI text, table cells, and workflow copy.

label.fontFamily: IBM Plex Sans, Noto Sans Thai Looped, system-ui, sans-serif
label.purpose: Controls, navigation, field labels, and filter labels.

meta.fontFamily: IBM Plex Sans, Noto Sans Thai Looped, system-ui, sans-serif
meta.purpose: text-meta 13/20: breadcrumbs, meta lines, table headers, hints and errors, status badge text, sm buttons, chips and menu trails.

metric.fontFamily: IBM Plex Sans, Noto Sans Thai Looped, system-ui, sans-serif
metric.purpose: text-metric 28/32, weight 500, -0.02em: stat values. Numbers only, always with num.

count.fontFamily: IBM Plex Sans, Noto Sans Thai Looped, system-ui, sans-serif
count.purpose: text-count 20/24, weight 600, -0.01em: counts in rows and compact stats. Numbers only, always with num.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: shadow-overlay: dialogs, sheets, popovers, dropdown menus and toasts only. Panels, cards, and the topbar are flat.

shadows.name: field-focus
shadows.purpose: shadow-field-focus: the halo around a focused field (with a 1px ring) and an open SearchableSelect. Not elevation.

shadows.name: field-error
shadows.purpose: shadow-field-error: the halo around an unfocused field with aria-invalid. Not elevation.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, selection, and state feedback only.

motion.name: menu-open
motion.value: 160ms ease-out fade + 4px slide in; 100ms fade out; no zoom
motion.purpose: Dropdown menus, submenus and popovers. motion-reduce:animate-none! turns it off.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable nonessential transitions for users who request reduced motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary action button (Button variant default) for save, create, submit, approve, or workflow-forward actions. Disabled and busy buttons turn grey with faint text instead of fading. A prerequisite gate is aria-disabled: it keeps focus, aria-describedby points at the visible line that says why, and its handler returns first; a rule about what the person typed never disables the save.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Secondary action (Button variant outline) for filters, navigation-adjacent actions, and lower-priority commands. Its #C3CDDA border is decorative; the label says it is a button.

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Standard form field (Input, NativeSelect or Textarea inside Field) for asset, employee, location, search, and settings fields. Panel fill, 3:1 border, focus halo, error through aria-invalid. The error line sits under the hint (13px danger text, no alert role), aria-describedby reads it first, and a save focuses the first wrong field.

components.name: Choice Card

components.description: AccessibleDialog with its parts: a header with the title and the ghost close X (named "ปิด"), a body in the panel color that scrolls, and a footer that stays in view on the background fill under a border-soft line. Secondary first, primary last: phones stack the buttons full width with Cancel on top, and from 640px they form a right-aligned row. On phones the box sits above the iPhone home bar. A field's error shows under its field in the body; an error of the dialog's action that names no field shows as a danger Notice at the top of the body.

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: One StatusBadge in one size (22px, 13/20 text, 6px corners) and two tiers with shape-coded markers. Calm tier (info ring, success/primary dot, neutral-ink bar): no fill or side padding, muted-foreground text. Attention tier (warning triangle, danger diamond): soft fill, border, 8px side padding and tone ink. Every badge carries a text label; database status colors are not shown. In high-contrast mode markers use the system text color.

components.name: Sidebar Navigation Item
components.description: RBAC-filtered row in the sidebar (three sections with headings). Full-width rounded row inside the nav's 8px (px-2) gutter (the margin below stands in for that gutter), sidebar-muted icon, Sidebar Hover; each section is role=group labelled by its heading. The active row is solid navy with white text and a teal icon, with an outline in Windows high-contrast mode; aria-current=page only on the exact page, aria-current=true on the entry above a detail page. Its focus ring sits outside the row on the sidebar color.

components.name: Tab Nav
components.description: TabNav: links that change the URL, named by their nav and marked with aria-current=page, not an ARIA tab list. One underline at every width: an inset line under the row and a 2px primary line under the current tab, which is weight 600. Counts are 13px tabular after the label (primary on the current tab). 40px tall from 768px and 44px below; the row scrolls sideways when it does not fit.

components.name: Stat Strip
components.description: StatStrip: the numbers above a list in one 12px frame with 1px lines between the cells and no status fill. A cell is a 13/500 label, the value in the Metric size with tabular figures, and an optional faint foot of at most two lines, which then ends in an ellipsis (its title holds the whole text). Two columns below 1024px, one row from 1024px. A cell that filters the list is one stretched link; the current one has primary-soft, a 2px primary line and aria-current=page. A cell that needs action has a warning foot line with its icon.

components.name: Row Actions
components.description: RowActions in a table row: one next-step button (120px wide, 13px medium primary text with a 16px icon, 32px tall from 768px and 44px below) that fills with primary-soft while its row is hovered or holds focus, plus a ghost icon button that opens a menu from 768px and a bottom sheet below. narrative.overview: This visual system should feel like a trusted enterprise record system for asset ownership, custody, audit, maintenance, disposal, reporting, and administration. It is structured, accountable, and operationally reliable. The interface serves real Thai corporate operations, so the design language is calm, corporate, data-driven, and practical.
keyCharacteristics: Dense enough for enterprise scanning, never cramped.
Bordered and tonal by default; only floating layers are lifted.
Status-rich, permission-aware, and readable in Thai and English.
Built for desktop administration and mobile field audit work.

rules.name: The Where Color Lives Rule
rules.body: Navy #083161 lives only in the logo and the selected menu row. Actions and links use Primary #1E4F94. Teal is for info status, the focus ring (#10858D) and the selected menu icon. Green, orange and red appear only inside status badges, as the icon of a toast, a Notice or an ActionEmptyState, and on destructive buttons and menu items; only warning and danger toasts and Notice boxes get a soft fill. Names are the neutral Chip, states StatusBadge and notes Notice by meaning, so outside the shared parts (the info status ring and the info Notice icon) no screen uses the info tokens (phase 2D).

rules.name: The Status With Evidence Rule
rules.body: Status cues must never rely on color alone. Pair semantic color with readable labels, marker shapes, consistent tone mapping, and visible workflow context.

rules.name: The No Decorative Gradient Rule
rules.body: Decorative gradients are prohibited. The product should feel like an enterprise operations system, not a landing page.

rules.name: The Token Contrast Rule
rules.body: Status text uses the status ink (text-success, text-warning, text-danger, text-info) on the panel, the page background, canvas, muted, accent, row-hover, or its own soft surface (bg-{tone}-soft). Never tint with opacity (bg-warning/10, bg-primary/10, border-warning/30, bg-muted/40) and never lighten solid fills on hover (/90): use the -soft, -border and -hover tokens and the solid neutrals (bg-background, bg-row-hover, border-border-soft). Faint text (#56677F) is AA on every neutral surface and on primary-soft, never on a status soft fill. tests/design-tokens-contrast.test.ts enforces every text pair at 4.5:1 and rings, field borders and meaningful icons at 3:1; button outlines are decorative.

rules.name: The Two-Theme Rule
rules.body: Two themes share one set of token names: light (each colorMeta canonical, each shadow value and the css examples here) and dark (each dark and darkValue). They live only in src/app/globals.css: the light :root block, :root[data-theme="dark"] and its identical copy under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark), one forced-light [data-theme="light"] scope and one print reset. The page follows the OS until the person chooses with the toggle beside the language button; the theme cookie keeps the choice per browser and the server renders it as data-theme on html, so the first paint is right. Components use tokens only: no dark: class and no @custom-variant dark. Paper (the A4 documents, the label sheet and its settings sample, the signature canvas) carries data-theme="light", QR tiles and the camera keep their own colors, and print is always light. Uploaded photos and logos sit on --image-stage #E9EEF5 in both themes; the app icon gets the --app-icon-frame hairline, #FFFFFF in light and #34496A in dark. In dark the solid fills take the dark ink #08172C, brand navy is only the pressed fill, and the contrast suite runs every rule on both sets.

rules.name: The No Display Labels Rule
rules.body: Never use display fonts, fluid hero type, or oversized marketing typography for labels, buttons, data, navigation, or form controls.

rules.name: The Thai Line-Height Rule
rules.body: text-sm is 22/14 in every language; Thai pages raise text-xs, text-xl, text-2xl and text-3xl to 18/12, 30/20, 36/24 and 44/30. text-meta (20/13) needs no Thai override; text-metric and text-count hold numbers only. A4 operation documents keep text-sm at 20/14 so the signature row stays on page 1.

rules.name: The Thai Readability Rule
rules.body: Thai and English labels must remain readable at operational density. Do not shrink helper text or placeholders below accessible contrast or touch usability.

rules.name: The Border First Rule
rules.body: Use a border and tonal surface for grouping. Panels, cards, sections, and the topbar are flat; only dialogs, sheets, popovers, menus, and toasts use shadow-overlay (dialogs and sheets over a bg-scrim backdrop). Six shadow-sm stay on controls over a camera image or photo and on paper previews, and two larger shadows on the round scan button and the register's phone bulk-action bar (phase 3); a guard holds exactly these 8 in its EXEMPT list.

rules.name: The No Floating Marketing Cards Rule
rules.body: Panels must not become decorative cards arranged for landing-page drama.

dos: Do preserve existing tokens and shared primitives such as Button, Segmented, the field primitives (Input, NativeSelect, Textarea, Field, SearchField), the dialog parts (AccessibleDialogBody, AccessibleDialogFooter, AccessibleDialogCancel) and useConfirm, StickyFormFooter and ActionBar, ChoiceCard and ChoiceChip, Chip, Steps, FormSection, FileQueueList, Notice, EmptyNote, ActionEmptyState, PageHeader and PageBackLink, DataTable with TableEmptyRow and Pagination, FilterSelect, FilterFormActions and FilterChipList, RowActions, TabNav, StatStrip, KeyValueList, ContentPanel divided, Nil, formatCount and formatMoney, the loading skeletons of page-skeleton.tsx, and the panel and mobile card list helpers.
Do keep navy #083161 for the logo and the selected menu row in the light theme, Primary #1E4F94 for actions and links, and teal for info status, focus and the selected menu icon.
Do use borders and tonal layers as the grouping mechanism; use shadow-overlay only for dialogs, sheets, popovers and menus, and bg-scrim behind them.
Do keep tables and forms dense enough for enterprise scanning, but not cramped.
Do pair status colors with readable labels, marker shapes, icons, or explicit workflow context so status does not rely on color alone.

Do support Thai and English text, keyboard navigation, visible focus states, reduced motion, touch-safe mobile/tablet controls, and clear empty, loading, error, permission-denied, and validation states.
Do check a form on save (noValidate and validate()), show each error under its field, take the person to the first wrong field and land the server's fieldErrors on the same fields.
Do preserve business workflows, RBAC, locale routing, audit trail expectations, Prisma/SQL Server behavior, and production readiness assumptions.
donts: Don't use consumer-app styling, bright playful colors, heavy animation, marketing-style hero layouts, gamified UI, casual startup dashboards, decorative gradients, or anything that makes the system feel like a landing page instead of an enterprise operations tool.
Don't use glassmorphism, heavy shadows, decorative gradients, floating marketing cards, or playful surfaces.
Don't bring back a dark navy sidebar in the light theme (the dark theme's chrome is its own token), a second focus color, or green, orange and red outside status badges.
Don't write a dark: class, a color for one theme or a component that reads the theme; paper that must stay light takes data-theme="light".
Don't show database status colors on badges, or use teal brand-accent as text.
Don't redesign business workflows for visual effect.
Don't invent inconsistent button, input, modal, badge, or navigation vocabularies across screens.
Don't rely on color alone for status, permission, validation, audit, or lifecycle state.
Don't use display fonts, fluid hero typography, gradient text, oversized cards, or landing-page composition inside product workflows.
Don't use colored side-stripe borders as a decorative accent. Use full borders, status badges, text labels, and icons instead.
Don't fade a disabled control with opacity, put faint text on a status soft fill, or tint a fill or border with /NN; use the disabled look, the tone ink and the solid tokens.

Don't change a button's label while it is busy, put the primary action first in the DOM (flex-col-reverse), drop required or maxLength from a control when it moves into Field, or give a dialog its own form when it renders inside another form.
Don't show a field's error in a toast or the browser's bubble, announce it as an alert, or keep a rule behind a disabled button with no reason on screen.

Don't write a page title, table head, sort header, empty row, pager, filter select, number box or label and value helper of your own, or bring back MetricCard, ReportHeader or MasterDataHeader: the list-frame guards (tests/list-frame-guards.test.ts, LH1 to LR1) allow only their shared parts (OWNERS) and the sites of their EXEMPT lists.
